concepts.title: Domain Restriction for Invertibility
concepts.definition: Trigonometric functions repeat their values, so they fail the one-one and onto test on their natural domains; trimming the domain to a well-chosen interval restores bijectivity and makes an inverse possible.
concepts.formula: restrict the domain so the map becomes one-one and onto
concepts.key_idea: Periodicity blocks an inverse; a restricted domain repairs the one-one and onto pairing that inversion needs.

solution_steps.explain: On the restricted domain the map is one-one and onto, so the inverse function exists.

concepts.title: Principal Value Branch of sin Inverse
concepts.definition: With sine restricted to the interval from minus pi by two to pi by two, the recovered map sends inputs from minus one to one back into that angle interval; this chosen branch is the principal value branch of inverse sine.
concepts.key_idea: Inverse sine maps [-1, 1] into [-pi/2, pi/2]; equal-length intervals such as [-pi, -pi/2] give other branches.

concepts.title: Principal Branch of cos Inverse
concepts.definition: Cosine restricted to the interval from zero to pi becomes bijective, and the recovered inverse cosine carries inputs from minus one to one into that same interval of angles.
concepts.key_idea: Inverse cosine outputs never leave [0, pi], so its principal values are never negative angles.

concepts.title: Principal Branches of tan Inverse and cot Inverse
concepts.definition: Tangent pinned to the open interval between minus pi by two and pi by two, and cotangent pinned to the open interval from zero to pi, both become bijective onto all real numbers; their inverses return angles inside those open intervals.
concepts.key_idea: Both inverses accept any real input; inverse tangent answers in (-pi/2, pi/2) while inverse cotangent answers in (0, pi).
concepts.textbook_ref: lemh102.txt, section 2.2 (tangent and cotangent discussion, lines 389-521)

concepts.title: Principal Branches of sec Inverse and cosec Inverse
concepts.definition: Secant and cosecant never output values strictly between minus one and one; after suitable restriction their inverses accept inputs outside that open band and return angles in trimmed intervals of length pi.
concepts.key_idea: Inputs must avoid the open band (-1, 1); the cosec inverse branch drops the angle zero and the sec inverse branch drops pi by two.

concepts.title: Principal Value Evaluation
concepts.definition: Evaluating an inverse trigonometric expression means converting it into a trigonometric equation, recalling the familiar angle with that ratio, and keeping it only when it falls inside the principal branch.
concepts.formula: principal value = the branch angle whose trigonometric ratio matches the input

concepts.title: Inverse Composition Property
concepts.definition: Inside matched domains and branches the function and its inverse cancel: sine applied to an arc sine returns the original number, while arc sine applied to a sine returns the original angle only when that angle already sits in the branch.
concepts.formula: sin(sin^-1 x) = x for x in [-1, 1]
concepts.key_idea: Cancellation is unconditional one way for x in [-1, 1]; the other way it holds only inside the principal branch.

concepts.title: Inverse Symbol versus Reciprocal
concepts.definition: The superscript minus one on sin^-1 x marks an inverse function, never a reciprocal; one divided by sin x is a different object with its own domain and behaviour.
concepts.formula: sin^-1 x is not 1 / sin x
concepts.key_idea: Arc sine finds an angle; the reciprocal of sine is a quotient, so the notation must never be mixed up.

concepts.title: Simplest Form by Substitution
concepts.definition: Expressions mixing radicals with inverse trig symbols collapse to one compact inverse trig term once a substitution such as x = sin theta or x = sec theta turns the radical into a standard identity.
concepts.formula: sin^-1(2x sqrt(1 - x^2)) = 2 sin^-1 x for x in [-1/sqrt 2, 1/sqrt 2]
concepts.key_idea: Substitute a trig parameter, apply a double angle or reciprocal identity inside, then cancel the inverse with its function.

concepts.title: Reducing Angles to the Principal Branch
concepts.definition: When the inner angle handed to an inverse trig function sits outside the principal branch, rewrite it with supplementary or periodic identities until the angle lands inside the branch; only then does cancellation apply.
concepts.formula: sin^-1(sin x) = pi - x for x in (pi/2, 3pi/2)
concepts.key_idea: Replace x by pi minus x (or shift by a period) so the inner angle enters the branch, as in sin of three pi by five equal to sin of two pi by five.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the principal value of sin inverse of one by two.

solution_template.explain: Let sin^-1(1/2) = y, so sin y = 1/2.
sin of pi by four equals one over root two; the angle with sine one half is pi by six.
pi by six lies in [-pi/2, pi/2], hence it is the principal value.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Evaluate sin inverse of sin of three pi by five.

solution_template.explain: Three pi by five is not in [-pi/2, pi/2], so direct cancellation is invalid.
sin of three pi by five equals sin of two pi by five.
Two pi by five lies in the principal branch, so the value is two pi by five.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Write cot inverse of one over root of x squared minus one in the simplest form for x greater than one.

solution_template.explain: Let x = sec theta with theta in the suitable interval.
Root of x squared minus one becomes tan theta, so the argument becomes cot theta.
cot inverse of cot theta is theta, and theta equals sec inverse x.
